chapter: 52nd Street, Birdland and the bop musicians
title: Miles Davis, the tuba and his troubles
summary: She credits a casual chat about tubas for Miles's nine-piece sound; she describes Miles in Birdland and what she heard of his later problems.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: No indeed. The only person I helped, Miles happened to be with me one day and Milton Oreny, the composer - he had so many masters in music till he couldn't play or write. Some people study too much. Milton and I were just saying a combination of things and I mentioned about a tuba and I think that that thing, that sound that Miles got on a record, was an idea of me just thinking of instruments, and he called me back and thanked me.
Was this when Miles had that 9-piece group?
Yes, that beautiful sound. We were all just sitting here naming instruments that we'd like to do things with, you know. He thanked me.
How about- you saw quite a bit of Miles, didn't you, during that period?

Oh, sure. We used to go to Birdland. It's the most peculiar thing to see him like he is now. I can't understand it. We'd be at Birdland and Miles had made some changes on Yesterday's. He'd say, "Look at this, Lou." You know, I'm a much better reader looking at music than I

am when I read it there, 'cause my mind starts wandering and I listen to the musicians and all that. It's a little confusing. He had brought in some changes on 'Yesterday.' I looked up at the stand and I looked at them. All of a sudden Fats Navarro, Charlie Parker, and all of them were so high until they had gone asleep. He said, "Look, look, Lou. I'd rather be something he is than to be in that condition." I understand a little later than that, maybe less than a year, Miles ran into Fats Navarro and Fats Navarro was out. Miles was so disgusted he said, "Man, give me that," and he went out with him. So that was the beginning of his drinking and whatnot. But he's a beautiful cat.
Do you see Miles at all these days?

No, but I like Miles. When I began praying Miles called me Reverend Williams and I gave him prayers and I sent him a lot of things. I played a concert with him in Europe about 3 years ago and he was all love and kisses and whatnot. I think he's very fond of me. I don't know what happened; I really don't know if all these things are as bad as some people say, but I think he became discouraged. I wasn't there but I heard during that period that I used to see him in Birdland, that Miles was abused by a policeman or something and he's been through several things like that. That can discourage one, you know what I mean, because if a man's outside catching the air and

trying to rest or do something like that and someone come up and abuse them for no reason whatsoever, well - I think a series of things like that happened to him to discourage him. I really don't know if he's as bad as what I hear, because I still like him and my brother Jerry is really crazy about him. I've had people to tell me to go down and see him. I said, "I don't want to go down and see him if he's in a bad way. He may not remember me as a person that he liked."
